extracted.intended_audience: journalists, journalism educators, newsroom managers, and health/mental-health professionals working with journalists
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and best-practice principles for reporting on trauma, conflict and tragedy and for supporting journalists' psychological resilience; guidance for newsrooms, educators and clinicians working together to improve trauma-aware reporting and duty of care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compassionate, ethical and professional reporting on victims and survivors
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocates for compassionate, ethical and professional reporting on victims and survivors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes reporting with sensitivity, dignity and respect; rooted in the Global Center’s mission to improve media coverage of trauma, conflict and tragedy. Historical precedent (MSU program) specifically trained journalism students to report on victims of violence with sensitivity, dignity and respect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trauma-aware reporting grounded in highest journalism standards and evidence-based trauma science
rubrics_metrics.description: Trauma-aware reporting should be grounded in both the highest standards of journalism practice and evidence-based trauma science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Global Center draws on an interdisciplinary network of news professionals, mental health experts, educators and researchers to provide reporters and filmmakers with the knowledge, skills and support necessary for trauma-aware reporting. Implies combining ethical journalistic practice with current clinical/research evidence about trauma effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foster psychological resilience and duty of care for journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Dedicated to the psychological resilience of journalists worldwide and fostering best practices in duty of care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes promoting resilience through training, newsroom peer support programs, workshops, fellowships and other supports. The Center’s work emphasizes protecting journalists’ mental health as part of professional practice and organizational responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance press freedom via research and education on trauma-facing reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Advance press freedom through research and education on the impact of trauma-facing reporting and dissemination of best practices to foster resilience in news professionals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research and education efforts should examine how trauma-facing reporting affects journalists and audiences and produce guidance that supports both ethical reporting and press freedom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a professional forum to share knowledge and strategies across all media
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a professional forum for journalists across all media to share knowledge and ideas, advance strategies related to effective, ethical reporting on violence and tragedy, and foster best practices in professional trauma awareness and duty of care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forum activities include convenings, workshops, public programs and cross-disciplinary conversations among journalists, clinicians and researchers to develop and spread effective strategies and best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain and publicly provide a comprehensive archive of resources and original content
rubrics_metrics.description: Make available a comprehensive archive of resources (including legacy Dart Center materials) alongside original content to serve the journalism community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a public service the GCJT website hosts the Dart Center archive plus new GCJT resources to support training, education and practice in trauma-aware journalism; signals importance of accessible, curated resource collections for practitioners and educators.
